questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The history of an Australian rock band
How electrical systems differ between countries
How to become an electrician
Why lightning is dangerous
questions.why: Neil says they'll find out how electricity differs across the world and why some systems are more complicated.

questions.q: What does Georgina first think Neil means by 'AC DC'?
options: A type of battery
A laptop brand
A science programme
A rock band
questions.why: She thinks he means the Australian rock'n'roll band.

questions.q: What has Georgina noticed when she travels abroad?
options: She needs a converter plug for her laptop
Her phone charges faster
Electricity is more expensive
Her laptop stops working completely
questions.why: She says she needs a converter plug to connect her laptop in another country.

questions.q: According to Keith Bell, what is unusual about Japan?
options: It has no standard frequency for its electricity
It uses only direct current in homes and offices
Part of it uses 60 hertz and part uses 50 hertz
It uses exactly the same system as the UK does
questions.why: He says one of the main islands is at 60 hertz and the other half of Japan is at 50 hertz.

questions.q: What does Keith Bell say about the mainland US?
options: It uses exactly 50 hertz everywhere in the country
It has three separate areas with slightly different frequencies
It changed its whole electrical system quite recently
Its frequency is exactly the same as Japan's
questions.why: He says there are three synchronous areas which, not being connected, run at slightly different frequencies.

questions.q: What problem does Gareth Mitchell have in the United States?
options: His laptop won't turn on at all over there
His phone gets very hot when he charges it
He can't find the right plug adaptor anywhere
His electric toothbrush doesn't charge properly
questions.why: He says his electric toothbrush doesn't charge up there, but his laptop still works.

questions.q: Why does Gareth's laptop still work in the US, according to Keith Bell?
options: American laptops are built to be much stronger
He always uses a special cable from the UK
It has a converter that doesn't care about frequency
Laptops don't really need electricity to charge
questions.why: He says laptop power supplies have a little converter designed not to care what frequency the input is.

questions.q: According to Neil, what is happening to these electrical anomalies?
options: They're becoming less common thanks to modern technology
They are getting worse and worse every year
They only affect old toothbrushes and clocks
Countries are finally agreeing on one frequency
questions.why: Neil says with modern technology these anomalies are becoming less and less commonplace.
